en: Dependent on a state that is not resultant (*navipāka*), a resultant state arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). Dependent on a state that is not resultant, a state with the nature of being resultant (*vipākadhammadhamma*) arises by way of root condition … five [combinations].

Dependent on a state with the nature of not being resultant (*navipākadhammadhamma*), a resultant state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state with the nature of not being resultant, a state that is neither resultant nor with the nature of being resultant (*nevavipākanavipākadhammadhamma*) arises by way of root condition … three [combinations].
Dependent on a state that is neither resultant nor with the nature of being resultant, a state that is neither resultant nor with the nature of being resultant arises … [by way of root condition].
Conditioned by root. Dependent on a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants, a resultant state arises by way of root condition...

five. (Abbreviated. Under root: twenty-two; under object: eleven; under predominance: eighteen... mutual: sixteen... prenascence: nine; repetition: six... resultant: fifteen... non-disappearance: twenty-two.
